summary:
The plan is a double cross: a north–south body crossed by three east–west bars, with two big planted courtyards and smaller courts between them. The wings are 12-storey flat-roofed blocks in beige smooth sandstone, with a grid of 3-block bays of recessed dark windows and about 1 in 6 lit. Every wing ends in a blank 13-storey squared tower, as in the photo.
In the middle, a stepped-up central block carries a floodlit penthouse and masts with red aircraft lights, and every roof is a lit slab deck behind a quartz coping line. The west front on Shifu Road has a quartz-columned canopy, the name, the city emblem and flagpoles, and the camera-facing south and east fronts get the most lit windows and floodlit tower panels.
